title: Git Rebase
overview: Git rebase moves or reapplies commits on top of another branch to create a cleaner project history.

example.title: Rebase Command
example.content:
git checkout feature

git rebase main

title: Git Stash
overview: Git stash temporarily saves uncommitted changes so developers can switch branches without losing work.

title: Git Reset
overview: Git reset moves the branch pointer and can be used to undo commits or remove staged changes.

example.title: Reset Types
example.content:
git reset --soft

git reset --mixed

git reset --hard

title: Git Revert
overview: Git revert creates a new commit that reverses the changes of a previous commit safely.

title: Git Tags
overview: Git tags mark specific points in repository history, commonly used for application releases.

title: Git Cherry Pick
overview: Git cherry-pick allows applying a specific commit from one branch to another branch.

title: Git Hooks
overview: Git hooks automatically execute scripts during specific Git actions like commit or push.

example.title: Hook Example
example.content:
Before Commit
 ↓
Run Validation
 ↓
Create Commit

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned advanced Git features including rebase, stash, reset, revert, tags, cherry-pick, and hooks.

example.content:
